answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by rooting reputation in an attested interaction graph: every completed task leaves a signed, stake-weighted edge, so a newcomer starts with no credit and must earn trust over a long voyage of real work. Fake identities arrive with no history and cannot conjure one cheaply, like a vine that needs seasons to grow roots. When a tide of sockpuppets floods the network, peers flag clusters whose shallow graph depth fails a minimum stake threshold, while established agents keep transacting. Mass identity fabrication becomes expensive and unprofitable.
